The table itself carries the tag `pii` and the policy uses `MATCH COLUMNS has_tag_value('pii','email')`. What is the likely cause?
choices: Column tags are not inherited from the table and MATCH COLUMNS checks column tags, so the email column needs the tag
ABAC policies only apply to tables created before the policy existed, so a new policy is needed for each new table
The table owner has to bind the policy to the table with ALTER TABLE ... SET MASK before the policy takes effect
Policies on catalogs are Beta and do not apply to schemas or tables that were created after the policy was made
quiz.explain: ABAC policies evaluate dynamically and cover new tables once the right tags exist. Table tags are not inherited by columns and MATCH COLUMNS reads column tags only. Table owners do not bind ABAC policies, and catalog-level policies on tables are not the Beta part.

days.recap: Masks (per column) and row filters (one per table) are SQL UDFs attached by owner or MANAGE+SELECT with EXECUTE on the function; use is_account_group_member. ABAC: governed tags plus a catalog-level policy with TO/EXCEPT cover many tables. Beta: metastore-level, DENY, views.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Weights and Commonly Confused Pairs

concepts.heading: Exam format and how code appears
concepts.body: The Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate exam has 45 scored multiple-choice questions, plus up to 10 unscored ones that are not marked, and a time limit of 90 minutes. The fee is USD 200, the certification is valid for 2 years, and there is no prerequisite. It is offered in English, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese and Korean, online proctored or at a test center, and no test aides are allowed. The pass mark is not published, so aim for a clear margin, for example around 80% in practice sets, rather than a minimum. The guide's sample questions are single answer, with no select-two format, so on test day expect exactly one best option per question. Code appears in SQL when possible and otherwise in Python (PySpark), in short snippets inside the stem or the options. You read code and decide what it does or what is wrong. The guide is updated from time to time, so check the current exam guide about two weeks before your date. The questions test the engineer's decision: which tool or option fits the data situation and why, not where to click. A scenario states the data, the requirement and a constraint such as least privilege, cost or idempotency, and the correct option is the one that satisfies all of them.

concepts.heading: Seven sections and how to spend your last hours
concepts.body: The exam covers seven sections with these weights: Databricks Platform 6%, Ingestion and Loading 21%, Transformation and Modeling 22%, Lakeflow Jobs 16%, CI/CD (Git folders and Declarative Automation Bundles) 10%, Troubleshooting, Monitoring and Optimization 10%, and Governance and Security 15%. Out of 45 questions that is roughly 3, 9, 10, 7, 4 to 5, 4 to 5 and 7 questions. Two sections, Ingestion and Transformation, together hold about 43% of the points, so a weak spot there costs the most. Governance is small but compact and very testable: privileges, managed versus external tables, masks, filters and ABAC. Platform is only 6%, so do not spend a day on it. For the last review, use this order: redo every quiz you missed, then read the confused pairs on this page, then do a timed set of 45 questions in 90 minutes. Treat mistakes by cause: a wrong fact (go back to that day), a misread condition (slow down on the stem), or a distractor that looked plausible (write down why it fails). Most distractors are correct tools in another situation.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs: ingestion, transformation and gold objects
concepts.body: COPY INTO versus Auto Loader: COPY INTO is a retriable, idempotent SQL command that skips loaded files and suits modest file counts; Auto Loader discovers new files incrementally with a checkpoint and scales to very large volumes. Directory listing versus file notification: listing is the default; file notification (managed file events) reads from a queue and avoids re-listing. availableNow versus processingTime: availableNow processes what is there and stops, ideal for scheduled incremental batch; processingTime keeps the query running; once is deprecated. addNewColumns versus rescue: evolution adds new columns, the rescued data column keeps values that do not fit the schema. UNION versus UNION ALL: UNION removes duplicates, UNION ALL keeps them and is cheaper; union matches columns by position, unionByName by name. explode drops rows with empty arrays; posexplode adds the position. Materialized view versus streaming table versus view: a materialized view stores a precomputed result and refreshes it; a streaming table processes append-only input once; a view stores only a query. Expectations versus constraints: expectations warn, drop or fail rows in a pipeline; NOT NULL and CHECK are enforced, PRIMARY KEY is not.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs: jobs, deployment, optimization and tables
concepts.body: Retry versus repair run: a retry re-runs a failed task automatically in the run, a repair re-runs failed tasks of a finished run; both restart the task, so make writes idempotent, for example MERGE. Run if versus If/else condition: Run if checks dependency outcomes (All done, At least one failed); If/else branches on a value comparison; For each loops over inputs. File arrival versus table update trigger: storage location versus Unity Catalog tables. Cooldown (minimum time between triggers) versus debounce (wait after last change): a debounce never fires under continuous arrivals; use a cooldown. Git folders versus bundles: Git folders handle workspace branches; Declarative Automation Bundles define jobs and pipelines as code, deployed with the CLI (validate, deploy, run, destroy). Development versus production mode: production validates settings and recommends a service principal as run_as. Skew versus spill: skew is uneven tasks (max far above the 75th percentile), spill is memory written to disk. OPTIMIZE versus OPTIMIZE FULL: incremental versus recluster everything after key changes. UNDROP versus RESTORE: UNDROP revives a dropped managed table within the recovery period; RESTORE rolls an existing table back.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs for governance, and a test-day plan
concepts.body: GRANT versus REVOKE versus DENY: access is additive in Unity Catalog; REVOKE removes a grant only where it was made, and SQL DENY exists only for hive_metastore (ABAC DENY policies are Beta). USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA navigate; SELECT reads. Owner versus MANAGE: both can grant; ALL PRIVILEGES excludes MANAGE. Column mask versus row filter: a mask changes a value in one column, a filter includes or excludes rows; both are SQL UDFs and a table has one row filter. is_account_group_member versus is_member: prefer the account-level function. Table-level masks versus ABAC: ABAC policies use governed tags and cover many and future tables. Metastore-level and DENY policies are Beta. Test-day plan: read the whole stem and find the requirement word (cheapest, least privilege, incremental, idempotent, without rewriting). Eliminate options that use a deprecated or wrong-scope tool, then compare the two left on the constraint. Answer every question; the guide does not describe a penalty for wrong answers, but check the current exam rules. Mark long code questions, move on, and return with the time left. Up to 55 questions can appear, so budget under 1.6 minutes each (about 82 minutes) and keep the rest for review.

examPoints: 45 scored single-answer multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes; pass mark unpublished; SQL first, PySpark otherwise; weights 6/21/22/16/10/10/15.
Ingestion (21%) and Transformation (22%) are the largest sections; Jobs (16%) and Governance (15%) follow.
Most distractors are right tools in the wrong situation: match the tool to the stated constraint (incremental, idempotent, least privilege, no rewrite).

quiz.q: A scheduled job must load only the files that arrived in cloud storage since the last run, from a location receiving millions of files, and stop afterwards. A teammate suggests a continuous streaming query with processingTime='1 minute' because it is simple. Which choice best fits the requirement?
choices: Keep processingTime='1 minute', since a continuous query is the only way to read incrementally
Use Auto Loader with the availableNow trigger and a checkpoint, run by the scheduled job
Use once=True, which Databricks recommends over availableNow for incremental batch workloads
Use COPY INTO on a job, because it is the best choice for millions of files in a location
quiz.explain: Auto Loader scales to very large file volumes and availableNow processes what is available and then stops, so the job ends. Once is deprecated, processingTime keeps running, and COPY INTO fits smaller file counts.

quiz.q: Production data of a payments table is governed in Unity Catalog. The group `contractors` was granted SELECT on the catalog and must now lose access to the schema `payments` only. A colleague proposes `DENY SELECT ON SCHEMA main.payments TO contractors`. What should the team do?
choices: Run the DENY, since it takes precedence over grants in Unity Catalog just as in the legacy metastore
Run REVOKE on the schema, which overrides the inherited catalog grant for that one schema only and keeps the rest
Run RESTORE on the schema, which reverts the privileges to the state they had before the catalog grant was made
Revoke the catalog grant and re-grant SELECT on the other schemas, because SQL DENY is for hive_metastore
quiz.explain: SQL DENY applies to hive_metastore only, and REVOKE removes a grant only at the level where it was made. Removing the catalog grant and granting at schema scope achieves the exception. RESTORE is a Delta table command.

days.recap: 45 scored single-answer questions, 90 minutes, SQL first, pass mark unpublished. Weights 6/21/22/16/10/10/15. Know the pairs: COPY INTO vs Auto Loader, view vs MV vs streaming table, retry vs repair, Git folders vs bundles, UNDROP vs RESTORE, REVOKE vs DENY, mask vs filter.
